## Scope

The series capstone: assembles the evidence from Books 01–18 into the
formal FedRAMP 20x authorization package — an OSCAL AP+AR+POA&M bundle,
the ConMon program that keeps evidence fresh post-ATO, and the BOD 26-04
VDR/VER submission due December 7, 2026. Thesis: **FedRAMP 20x replaces
the ~323-control Rev 5 Moderate baseline audit with a KSI-evidence model, so authorization becomes
a repeatable, machine-generated artifact sustained by cadenced monitoring**
rather than a one-time paperwork event.

## Learning objectives

- Enumerate the FedRAMP 20x package components (OSCAL SSP/AP/AR/POA&M,
  evidence books, VDR, training record) and their sources.
- Generate and validate the OSCAL 1.0.4 bundle and explain the
  AP→AR→POA&M UUID linkage.
- Operate the CA-7 ConMon calendar across monthly, quarterly,
  semi-annual, and annual cadences.
- Run the BOD 26-04 pipeline (Syft → Grype → OpenVEX via vexctl) and
  submit VDR/VER to CISA per format and deadline.
- Apply the eight-slot evidence freshness rules and interpret the four
  Sentinel ConMon workbooks.
- Map OSCAL AR risk entries into the PM-9 risk register and name residual
  risks outside KSI scope.
- Execute the AO pre-submission checklist and day-of-submission procedure.

## Key concepts

- The OSCAL bundle: `ksi-ap.json`, `ksi-ar.json`, `ksi-poam.json`,
  `artifact-index.json`.
- The 29/29 KSI scorecard (self-assessed against the series' internal KSI
  decomposition, pending CR26 reconciliation and independent SCA): 10 rules via the CISA
  ScuBA adapter (KSI-001..010), 19 via the AAN slot evaluator (KSI-011..029).
- Zero-item POA&M as the correct target state, with automatic gap
  extraction populating entries when a verdict slips.
- Ten KSI themes mapped to the eight evidence slots.
- BOD 26-04 artifact chain: Syft CycloneDX 1.6 → Grype VDR → OpenVEX VER
  → CISA submission.
- Per-slot evidence freshness rules with named owners; four Sentinel
  ConMon workbooks (KSI Status, Control Drift, Vulnerability Backlog,
  Training Coverage).
- Authorization timeline: Class A Aug 3 / Class B+C Aug 31 2026; 20x
  mandatory Jan 1, 2027.

## Deliverable sequence (artifact-shaped)

1. Generate the OSCAL bundle; confirm 29/29 self-assessed satisfied against the
   series' internal KSI decomposition (pending CR26 diff + SCA) and a zero-item POA&M as
   the target state; archive to history.
2. Compile and upload the evidence books with a book→controls→KSI
   cross-reference index.
3. Run the BOD 26-04 pipeline; draft VEX for CVSS ≥ 7.0; submit to CISA by
   December 7, 2026.
4. Export and threshold-check the training-effectiveness-record (≥95%,
   six tiers, dates within 12 months).
5. Stand up ConMon: Sentinel dashboard, monthly AR automation, quarterly
   review in the PM-14 plan, ISSO in the PM-2 RACI.
6. Day of submission: final bundle, timestamped archive, structure
   validation, ZIP for the FedRAMP PMO.

Once the package is operating, track the
[post-implementation KPIs](../assessment-rubrics.html#post-implementation-kpis)
— outcome thresholds read from the same evidence surfaces the ConMon
calendar keeps fresh.

## Compliance hooks

CA-2, CA-5, CA-6, CA-7, CA-7(1), CA-7(3), RA-3, SA-15; SR-11 for
BOD 26-04. Cadence tables also cite AT-2/AT-4, CP-2/CP-3, IR-2, RA-5,
AC-6, AU-6, SI-4, SR-5/SR-6, PM-2/PM-9/PM-14. FedRAMP 20x: all 29 internal KSI-decomposition rules
KSIs enumerated across the ten themes.

## Prerequisites

All of Books 01–18; leans specifically on Book 13 (Sentinel dashboard),
Book 14 (CP tabletops), Book 15 (SBOM/VDR pipeline), Book 16 (PM-9
register, PM-14 plan), and Book 18 (training record).

## Labs

1. Generate the OSCAL bundle, then trace the AP→AR→POA&M UUID links and
   verify the 29 finding verdicts programmatically.
2. Execute the full Syft → Grype → vexctl chain against a sample container
   and assemble a mock CISA VDR submission package.
3. Simulate a training-completion drop below 95%, regenerate the bundle,
   and observe automatic POA&M creation and the CA-7(3) trend signal.

## Pitfalls the book calls out

- Zero open KSI risks does not eliminate enterprise risk — mission,
  insider-threat, physical, and geopolitical supply-chain risks sit
  outside KSI scope.
- A downward trend in the satisfied count must trigger a POA&M entry;
  stale AR history breaks the CA-7(3) early warning.
- Evidence goes stale silently — each slot has explicit freshness
  requirements (e.g., SBOM within 90 days at submission) that ConMon must
  enforce.
- The book's own closing disclaimer: control-closure claims are advisory
  pending formal FedRAMP PMO / AO review — the package is not an ATO.
